changes.text: 光绪元年，左宗棠刚平定关陇，大军正要出关，海防之议先起了。论者说，自高宗定新疆，「歲糜數百萬，此漏卮也」，如今「竭天下力贍西軍，無以待不虞」，不如照英国人的主张办：「許帕夏自立為國稱籓，罷西征，專力海防」。

In the first year of the Guangxu reign, Zuo Zongtang had just pacified Guanlong, and his army was about to march out beyond the pass when the argument over coastal defense broke out first. Since the emperor Gaozong took Xinjiang, critics said, "several million a year have drained away, a leaky vessel"; now things had reached the point of "exhausting the strength of the whole realm to feed the western army, leaving nothing for the unforeseen." Better to do as the British proposed: "let Pasha found his own state and pay homage as a vassal, call off the western expedition, concentrate on coastal defense."

Before judging whether to stop, look at what the western spending was protecting. The Muslim chief beyond the frontier whom the biography calls Pasha was by origin a hoşbeg of the Andijan. Andijan had belonged to Kokand; Russia destroyed Kokand, and Andijan alone survived. Pasha, the record says, "feared Russian pressure and slipped across the border." Inside it he took Kashgar, nibbled away at the eight southern cities, and defeated Tuo Ming, the Muslim holding Ürümqi, so that he also possessed the Ili cities of the north and took their taxes. He commanded the Muslim population, kept envoys moving to draw in British and Russian support, and bought arms: "The English secretly helped him, wishing to set him up as a separate state, to serve as a buffer against Russia."
北边动手更快。传记记为「當是時」，未系具体年份：俄以回数扰其边境，遽引兵逐回，取伊犁，且言将代取乌鲁木齐。

The north moved faster. The biography dates this only as "at that time," without naming a year: because the Muslims had repeatedly raided its border, Russia promptly sent troops to drive them out, took Ili, and said it would also take Ürümqi on China's behalf.
海防一派的主张写得直白：西征是填不满的漏卮，一旦有不虞之事将无以应对，不如许帕夏自立为国、向中国称籓，把力量全数转去海防。传记说「鴻章言之尤力」，却没有记下鸿章本人的具体论据；赞成一方的理由在史料里仅存「論者多言」一段概述。

The coastal-defense case was stated flatly: the expedition was a vessel with a hole in it, and if anything unforeseen came, nothing would be left to meet it. Better to let Pasha set up a tributary state and turn every resource to the coast. The biography says "Hongzhang pressed this hardest of all" (the record gives only the name Hongzhang), but records none of his own specific arguments; for that side of the debate, the record preserves only one summary paragraph of the proponents' case.

作者认为，左宗棠的反驳重心在账上，不过原话里也有「挫國威」这样的非财务理由。他认为割弃不等于省钱：关陇新平，不趁势收回旧地，反而让帕夏另立一国，是坐自遗患；帕夏若守不住，地不是归英就是入俄，地盘坐缩，边防要地尽失，防边的兵也减不掉。传记记其言：「關隴新平，不及時規還國家舊所沒地，而割棄使別為國，此坐自遺患。萬一帕夏不能有，不西為英並，即北折而入俄耳。吾地坐縮，邊要盡失，防邊兵不可減，糜餉自若。無益海防而挫國威，且長亂。此必不可。」要害在中段：兵减不掉，饷照旧要花。

One reading is that Zuo's answer rested chiefly on cost, though his words also cite damage to the state's prestige. Carving territory loose, he argued, did not save money: it stored up trouble, and if Pasha failed to hold the land it would fall to England or to Russia; the territory would shrink, every strategic point be lost, and the frontier troops could not be cut. The biography gives his words: "Guanlong has only just been pacified. Instead of recovering in good time the lands the state once lost, we carve them off and let another state be founded there — that is to store up trouble of our own making. Should Pasha fail to hold them, they will be swallowed by England in the west or fold north into Russia. Our territory shrinks of its own accord, every strategic point is lost, the frontier troops cannot be reduced, and the spending goes on as before. It does nothing for coastal defense, it damages our prestige, and it feeds disorder. This must not be." The sting is in the middle: the troops cannot be cut, and the money flows out all the same.
关于争论如何收场，传记记得很简短。军机大臣文祥独善宗棠议，遂决策出塞，不罢兵，授左宗棠钦差大臣督军事，金顺副之。传记只记文祥一人赞成，未记其理由。

The record of how it ended is brief. Wenxiang, a Grand Council minister, was the only one to favor Zuo's plan; the decision went to march beyond the pass rather than halt the campaign, with Zuo named Imperial Commissioner for military affairs and Jin Shun as his deputy. The biography records only that Wenxiang agreed, and no reason why.

The call to stop came a second time. The minister at Kulun reported that the western question should be settled by fixing a frontier, and courtiers argued the expedition cost too much: with Ürümqi and Turpan in hand, the army could rest. Zuo sighed: "The moment offers an opening — and we would settle for drawing lines on the map and shrinking back?" He sent up a forceful memorial against it; the throne agreed.
还有一层分寸。时俄方与土耳其战，金顺请乘虚袭伊犁，宗棠曰：「不可。師不以正，彼有辭矣。」随后大军还定乌什，收南疆东四城，何步云以喀什汉城降；伯克胡里既纳白彦虎，乃效力攻汉城，大军至，复遁走俄；西四城相继下，宗棠露布以闻，诏晋二等侯。

There was also the matter of restraint. Russia was then at war with Turkey, and Jin Shun asked leave to strike Ili while it lay open. "No," said Zuo. "An army that does not act by right hands them their excuse." The army turned back to reduce Ushi, then took the four eastern cities of the south, and He Buyun surrendered the Chinese city of Kashgar. Bokhuli, having taken in Bai Yanhu, then threw his strength against that Chinese city; when the army arrived, he fled again into Russia. The four western cities fell in turn; Zuo announced the victory by public dispatch, and an edict raised him to second-class marquis.

The author's inference is that, set side by side, the two lines show one test: recover the ground, but leave no handle for the other side. In the first year of Guangxu the fear was that cession would damage prestige and feed disorder; here, that an army acting without right would hand Russia its excuse. One reading is that he judged a move by whether it could be held afterwards and defended in argument, not by the land it gained. The biography draws no such conclusion.

With north and south recovered, the question shifted from whether to fight to how to hold. In the first month of the fourth year Zuo laid out plans to make Xinjiang a regular province and asked that Russia be negotiated with over two things: the return of Ili and the surrender of fugitives. A plenipotentiary envoy, Chong Hou, was sent to Russia. Russia pressed three demands — trade, boundaries, indemnity — and Chong Hou signed at once. Court officials impeached him, and the matter stayed open for a long time.

Chong Hou was disgraced and removed, and Zeng Jize sent to Russia to revise the treaty. Zuo asked to move out to Hami to prepare the recovery of Ili. In the fourth month of the sixth year he set out from Suzhou "carrying his coffin" and reached Hami in the fifth. Russia, hearing the imperial army was moving in force, reinforced Ili and the Naryn and put warships to sea to shake the capital; Tianjin, Fengtian and Shandong were all on alert. In the seventh month Zuo was summoned to the capital as an adviser, with Jintang replacing him; the biography says Russia too was cowed by our military prestige. In the first month of the following year peace was concluded, Ili returned, and the coastal forces stood down.

In practice the ledger came down to logistics. Zuo "was quick to judge the moment in war and never kept to one set of tactics," and in western affairs he made saving troops and filling the stores his first principle. Twenty months beyond the pass, and every city in north and south recovered: the biography credits the abundance of supply. There was garrison farming too. He argued for military colonies early on and was thought pedantic; then he set out the abuses of the old garrisons inside and outside the pass — men on the army rolls who could not also farm — and proposed dividing the two, keeping the strong as soldiers, settling the meek and the weak on the land. Then people respected the long view behind it.
仗打赢之后，外部的看法也变了。国家承平久，武备弛不振，海外诸国虽见中国屡平大难，仍私议以为脆弱；及宗棠平帕夏，外国乃稍稍传说之。左宗棠初入京师时，内城有教堂高楼俯瞰宫殿，民间讙言「左侯至，樓即毀矣」；后出示谕晓，传言乃止，原文未明言示谕者是谁。

After the victories, opinion abroad shifted. The empire had been at peace so long that its armaments had gone slack, and the overseas powers, talking of wealth and strength among themselves, still whispered that China was frail even after it had put down one great crisis after another. Once Zuo had dealt with Pasha, the foreigners began to spread the word about him. When Zuo first entered the capital, a church tower in the Inner City overlooked the palace, and popular rumor had it that the tower would come down once the Marquis Zuo arrived; a notice was posted to explain, and the talk stopped. The record does not say who issued the notice.

The author's reading is that unpacking that first-year argument yields three reusable tests: can what you were protecting still be held once you stop? Is the money you save actually saved? Does the cost of delay simply pass to whoever comes next? One reading is that Zuo's objection held not because the expedition was worth more, but because cession left the cost structure untouched — less territory, the same troops, the same spending, and trouble added. That is the author's summary; the biography records events only.
本文全部史实出自《清史稿·左宗棠传》一处传记，成书刊行远在事件之后，是单一史源；没有同时期奏疏原文、上谕原件，也没有鸿章（原文只称其名）、帕夏、俄方、崇厚一方的记载可作对勘。文中的宗棠曰、歎曰，以及那道令曰，都是史家记述，未必是逐字原话；英文版中的引语均为作者自文言译出。文祥独善宗棠议、鸿章言之尤力各只有一句，未记具体论据，本文没有替任何一方补写心理动机。

Every fact here comes from a single source: the biography of Zuo Zongtang in the Draft History of the Qing, compiled and printed long after the events it describes. There are no contemporary memorials in their original form, no edicts to check against, and no account from Hongzhang (the record gives only this name), Pasha, the Russian side, or Chong Hou to set against it. The "Zuo said," "Zuo sighed," and the general order are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. All quotations in the English text are the author's translations from the classical Chinese. Wenxiang's support and Hongzhang's advocacy each appear in a single sentence, without their arguments, and no motive is written in for either.
全文仅据《清史稿·左宗棠传》单一史源，成书远晚于事件，无同期奏疏、上谕或对方记载可作对勘；引语为史家记述，未必逐字，英文版引语为作者译文；数字照录、口径不详；纪年不换算公元；「帕夏畏俄逼」为原文表述；替代选择与现代场景均为作者所加。

Everything rests on a single source, the biography of Zuo Zongtang in the Draft History of the Qing, compiled long after the events; there are no contemporary memorials, edicts or opposing accounts to check against. Quotations are the historian's rendering and may not be verbatim, and English quotations are the author's translations; numbers are reproduced as written, with scope unstated; dates are not converted out of the Guangxu reign years; "Pasha feared Russian pressure" is the source's own phrasing; and the modern scenes and the alternative option are the author's additions.

dispositions.rationale: 英文把 the Qianlong emperor 改为 the emperor Gaozong，与原文「高宗」直接对应；删去证据之外的地理注释 the Gansu–Shaanxi corridor。

evidence.quote: 論者多言自高宗定新疆

dispositions.rationale: record 段中“钱只有这么多……得当场回答”一句是作者框定，证据未载。中英两版都已删去该句，其余引文保持不变。

evidence.quote: 宜徇英人議，許帕夏自立為國稱籓，罷西征，專力海防

dispositions.rationale: 删去 'a title, roughly governor' 和 'or clan chief' 两处证据外的释义，只保留 Pasha 与 hoşbeg。

evidence.quote: 本安集延部之和碩伯克也

dispositions.rationale: 中文恢复为“且言将代取乌鲁木齐”，删去“也在其口头计划之内”；英文改为 said it would also take Ürümqi on China's behalf，保留“代”字的意思。
删去“到光绪元年”这一系年断言，改为说明传记只记「當是時」、未系具体年份，英文同步修改。

evidence.quote: 當是時，俄以回數擾其邊境，遽引兵逐回，取伊犁

dispositions.rationale: “海上一旦有事”改为“一旦有不虞之事”，英文改为 if anything unforeseen came, nothing would be left to meet it，不再把不虞限定为海上之事。
英文去掉证据外的姓氏 Li，改作 Hongzhang，并注明原文只称其名。
“不在道德，而在账”改为明确标注的作者解释：作者认为反驳重心在账上，并承认原话也有「挫國威」这一非财务理由。英文同步为 One reading is that... rested chiefly on cost。

evidence.quote: 無益海防而挫國威，且長亂

dispositions.rationale: 英文概述补上“坐自遗患”与“帕夏守不住则归英入俄”两层意思；译文改为 Instead of recovering in good time，补出“不及時”。

evidence.quote: 不及時規還國家舊所沒地
不西為英並，即北折而入俄耳

dispositions.rationale: 英文改为 The record of how it ended is brief，中文同步改为“关于争论如何收场，传记记得很简短”，去掉时长判断；'rather than disband' 改为 'rather than halt the campaign'。
删去证据外的地名对应 Khüree 与 Urga，只按「庫倫大臣」作 The minister at Kulun。

evidence.quote: 適庫倫大臣上言西事宜畫定疆界

dispositions.rationale: 按原文顺序重排为：何步云降，伯克胡里纳白彦虎后攻汉城，大军至后遁走俄，然后西四城相继下。补出伯克胡里攻汉城一事；遁走俄的主语只写伯克胡里，删去白彦虎同逃的推断。中英同步。

evidence.quote: 伯克胡里既納白彥虎，乃效力攻漢城。大軍至，复遁走俄。西四城相繼下

dispositions.rationale: 英文首句加上 The author's inference is that，与中文的“作者推断”一致。
「全權大臣」改译为 A plenipotentiary envoy，与左宗棠的 Imperial Commissioner（欽差大臣）区分开。

evidence.quote: 詔遣全權大臣崇厚使俄

dispositions.rationale: 删去证据外补写的动机 'meaning to die on campaign'，只保留 carrying his coffin。
「願弱」改译为 the meek and the weak，不再误作“愿意”。
删去证据未记的“后来”，改为“左宗棠初入京师时”，与英文 When Zuo first entered the capital 对应。
中文改为“后出示谕晓，传言乃止”，并注明原文未明言示谕者；民间传言改为直引「左侯至，樓即毀矣」。英文改为 the tower would come down once the Marquis Zuo arrived; a notice was posted，并注明未载示谕者，去掉左宗棠的主动意图。
